issues.description: The solution repository's PersonResource constructor has the wrong parameter type and does not initialize the personService field (it takes a NoteService and sets personService to null). The template and problem statement expect PersonResource to receive a PersonService and initialize the private final personService field. This constructor mismatch in the solution is structural and will cause NullPointerExceptions and confusion when students compare the template instructions with the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the solution's PersonResource to accept a PersonService parameter and assign it to the personService field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Ensure the constructor signature and initialization match the template and problem statement.

issues.description: The PersonResource dependency injection constructor is inconsistent between template and solution: the template (and problem description) expect a PersonService to be injected and assigned to the personService field, but the solution's PersonResource constructor declares a NoteService parameter and assigns personService = null. This mismatches the same conceptual entity (the PersonService dependency) across artifacts and will confuse students about which service should be provided to PersonResource and how to wire it.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution, change the PersonResource constructor to accept a PersonService and assign it to the field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } This aligns the constructor parameter name/type with the template and the problem specification.
